title: Redwood migration demo - OpenAI/Anthropic/Together parity mapping
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Atlas Retail through a migration-focused demo mapping OpenAI/Anthropic/Together API calls to Redwood equivalents, covered Console observability, Optimize cost/perf recommendations, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, and security controls (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Customer expressed interest in a pilot for product search reranking and conversational support; asked for pricing, security docs, and a benchmarking kit for throughput/latency comparison.
topics: Deployment choices: hosted vs dedicated vs private(VPC)
Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML
Next steps: pilot scope, pricing, benchmark run

header: Date: 2026-07-18 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Morales (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Atlas CTO), Priya Rao (Atlas Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Atlas Security)
transcript: 00:00 Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm samir from redwood, i'll kick us off - jenna will do the technical walkthrough. 00:07 Alex: yeah thanks, excited to see how this maps from our current openai setup. 00:12 Jenna: cool quick agenda, api parity, console + optimize, deployment options, security, and then q&a. 00:20 Priya: our main goal is parity for generative search reranking and chat support, we want minimal prompt changes and predictable latency under load. 00:30 Jenna: understood - we'll show two migration patterns: (1) drop-in API mapping for request/response parity, and (2) optimized route using redwood batching + kv-cache for cost/latency. 00:45 Samir: just to call out, customers often start hosted then move to dedicated when throughput grows; we'll show both. 00:53 Marcus: quick security callout: we need SOC2, KMS, audit logs and SSO. any red flags? 00:59 Jenna: we support SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS integration for private deployments, and detailed audit logs in the console - i'll share the pack after the call. 01:10 Priya: ok demo time? show us the API mapping first. 01:14 Jenna: sure, live screen - here is a sample openai call (gpt-4 style) side-by-side with redwood python and curl snippets. 01:24 Jenna: openai: POST /v1/chat/completions with model gpt-4, messages array. redwood parity: POST /v1/responses with model: "redwood/gpt4-equivalent" and messages in the same shape, we added a shim so message role/name mismatch rarely breaks. 01:45 Priya: nice - what about function calling differences? 01:48 Jenna: we map function call payloads; semantics are the same, redwood returns function_call object and we support streaming and tool-calls. small naming differences in metadata - we included a tiny helper lib in the sample repo. 02:05 Alex: any changes to rate limits or token accounting? 02:09 Samir: behavior mirrors per-customer limits; pricing unit is per-token like you're used to, but we expose more granular token breakdowns in console, and optimize can suggest batching to lower units. 02:25 Jenna: moving to console - shows dashboard - routes, per-route cost, per-model latency, token distribution. here's how you pin a route to a model and set a canary rollout (demo). 02:40 Jenna: also show tracing hooks - you can click a request and see token-by-token latency and whether it hit the prefix cache. 02:52 Priya: that cache thing - would that require changes to our prompts? 02:55 Jenna: generally no; prefix caching benefits repeated prefixes. for reranking we see big wins when top-K prefixes repeat. 03:05 Samir: Optimize module: suggests batch sizes, when to enable quantized variants, and a recommended model variant for your workload to balance 99th pct latency and unit cost. 03:18 Priya: do you auto-quantize models? 03:21 Jenna: we provide validated quantization profiles and recommend them in Optimize; the runtime has quantization-friendly kernels, but we don't alter model weights in hosted without a customer's sign-off. 03:35 Marcus: concerns about data residency and private deployments - can we run in our VPC? 03:40 Jenna: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC peering or on-prem package; KMS/HSM integrations for key control. audit logs available in the private control plane. 03:52 Alex: performance - we run 300 rps at peak for search reranking (each request 3-5 short prompts). can redwood handle that with single-digit tail latency? 04:02 Samir: depends on model variant and batching policy; for short prompts we can use continuous batching and a dedicated GPU pool; our customers hit 5-20ms per-token tail with optimized kernels for short sequences. we'll run a benchmark with your sample traces. 04:20 Priya: mapping for anthropic/together models - we use claude for some tasks and together.ai models for embeddings. is that supported? 04:30 Jenna: yes we maintain an internal catalog mapping: claude-2 -> redwood/claude-compat, together's models map to redwood/together-compat; embeddings are exported with same dimensionality and we expose compatibility wrappers. little differences sometimes in temperature semantics but the helper lib includes normalization. 04:50 Alex: can you demo a full migration example for our reranker - show a code diff? 04:55 Jenna: yes - opens sample repo - shows a tiny patch: swap client.openai.ChatCompletion.create -> redwood.responses.create, update model string, add a small adapter for function results. 05:12 Jenna: demo shows minimal code changes (2-4 lines in typical integrations) and includes tests we provide for result parity checks. 05:25 Priya: great. any limits on streaming or token length? 05:28 Jenna: we support streaming and long-context models; the runtime will select kernels based on seq length. for extremely long contexts we recommend dedicated or private where you can pin resources. 05:40 Marcus: audit trail and access controls - how granular is RBAC? 05:44 Jenna: role-based controls down to route level, SSO mappings, and API keys with scoped permissions. logs include request metadata and model variant used. 05:56 Alex: what about fallback policies - if a model is down or capacity constrained? 06:00 Samir: you can configure policy-based routing: prefer fast model, fallback to cheaper/compatible variant, or fall back to another region. for critical paths you can pin to dedicated capacity to avoid noisy neighbor issues. 06:13 Priya: curious about cost comparisons - how much cheaper is it? 06:17 Samir: workload dependent; with batching, cache hits, and quantized kernels we've seen 30-60% per-token cost reduction vs raw hosted gpt-4 class endpoints in our benchmarks. we'll run your traces to give a precise estimate. 06:35 Jenna: security docs note: encryption at rest, in transit, and optional customer-managed keys for private deployments; we'll share SOC2 report and penetration test summary. 06:49 Alex: ok big ask - we want a benchmark that mirrors our production 24h window, can you run that? 06:55 Samir: yes - next step is drop your sample traces, we'll provision a trial workspace and run a redwood vs openai/anthropic/together comparison, including latency p99 and cost per 1M requests. 07:08 Priya: do you need credentials/access? 07:10 Samir: just the traces and a short config file, we give you a script to anonymize sensitive fields. 07:18 Marcus: last question: legal and procurement - do you support standard enterprise SLAs and templates? 07:22 Samir: yes we have standard enterprise SOWs and SLA tiers; our legal team can start once pilot is greenlit. 07:30 Alex: sounds good. let's recap. 07:32 Samir: recap - send pricing & pilot SOW (samir), Jenna sends security pack + parity repo, priya sends traces, we schedule benchmark week of 7/27. 07:45 Alex: thanks everyone. 07:47 Samir: thanks, we'll follow up shortly.
